questions.q: Which chart title best follows this lesson's advice?
options: Sum of Amount
Open pipeline by stage
Chart 1
Opportunity report output
questions.explain: A title should state the point of the chart in plain language, not repeat the raw field or measure name.

questions.q: A summary report has hundreds of detail rows but managers only care about group totals. What formatting choice serves them best?
options: Add more columns so nothing is hidden
Convert it to a tabular report
Turn detail rows off so subtotals and the grand total stand out
Remove the grouping entirely
questions.explain: Collapsing detail rows makes a summary report read like a scorecard. Detail rows are more like an audit trail.

questions.q: Why combine small groups into 'Others' on a donut chart?
options: Salesforce cannot draw more than three slices
It avoids a dozen unreadable slivers and keeps the chart legible
It permanently deletes the small groups from the report
It changes the underlying report filter
questions.explain: Combining small groups is a display choice that improves readability; the report data is unchanged.

questions.q: Where is conditional highlighting available, per this lesson?
options: On summary fields in summary and matrix reports
Only on tabular reports
Only on dashboards
Only in Classic
questions.explain: Conditional highlighting applies color ranges to a summary field in summary and matrix reports in Lightning.

questions.q: What is the main risk of coloring every value in a report?
options: The report will refuse to save
Colors change the underlying data
Nothing stands out, and color alone may not be readable for everyone
Salesforce limits reports to one color
questions.explain: Highlighting only works as emphasis. Overuse removes the contrast, and color should never be the sole signal.
